# EBMC regression suite contract (opt-in)

These tests compare sva2yosys with the **known answers** of an external corpus: the SVA regression tests of EBMC, `regression/verilog/SVA` of https://github.com/diffblue/hw-cbmc at commit `2a3263c66d042364769353ea0b068ea1f5eec54e` (tag `ebmc-6.1`, BSD-3-Clause). The corpus is **not** part of this repository. A local checkout lives outside it; `tests/support/corpora.py` fetches it (pinned, sparse on that directory):

```text
uv run python tests/support/corpora.py C:/corpora ebmc
```

`SVA2YOSYS_EBMC_TESTS` names the directory (`.env.example`). The tests run only when the run selects the corpus and the tools they use: `--external-corpora=ebmc` (or `all`), `--external-tools=sby` (and `sby-live` for the cases with a liveness part, `yosys` for the version check), or `all`; otherwise they are skipped with a reason naming the switch. The shared rules of the external areas (`../CONTRACT.md`) apply.

**EBMC itself is never run.** What the corpus gives is the expected output of each test, in a `.desc` file (the tag, the design, EBMC's options, and one line per property such as `[main.p0] ...: PROVED up to bound 10`), next to the design `.sv`. These answers encode EBMC's own semantics; they are compared with ours and are never taken as ground truth (`../CONTRACT.md` 5). `fixtures/expectations.txt` is the classification, written by hand from a draft run (`tests/support/ebmc_corpus.py --draft`), and records for each property of each case the class below.

## What is compared

1. **The corpus is the classified one, and every case is listed.** The table's `corpus-sha256:` line is the SHA-256 of all the `.desc` and `.sv` files of the corpus (names and contents, line ends normalised to LF, in name order); `corpus-commit:` and `ebmc-version:` record the revision and the EBMC release whose answers they are. A checkout with other content fails until every case is classified again and the line updated. The digest is checked once per session by a fixture on which every corpus test of this area depends: on another revision they all fail (they do not skip) with one message to fetch the pinned commit or reclassify; the digest test itself checks it directly and is the representative. Every `.desc` of the corpus is listed, no listed case is missing from the corpus, and a case that is not skipped as a whole has one line per expected property line, in order, with the property's label.
2. **The tools are the classified ones.** The table records the OSS CAD Suite release, the Yosys version and the SBY version with which it was classified. The Yosys version of the configured `yosys` is checked against the table in a test of its own; another version fails it with the instruction to reclassify (SBY has no version query; it is recorded for the record).
3. **Which cases are compared (CORE).** Only cases tagged `CORE` are compared; tags such as `KNOWNBUG` mark cases that EBMC itself does not pass. A case is skipped as a whole, with its reason in the table, when EBMC rejects its input (`EXIT=2`), when an option tests EBMC itself (output formats, `--aig`, `--smv-word-level`, ...), when the source uses several clock events, or when no property has a known answer. A property has a known answer when EBMC's line is `PROVED`, `PROVED up to bound N` or `REFUTED` (for a cover: reached, or not reached within the bound); assumptions, engine refusals and `INCONCLUSIVE` have none and are skipped. Immediate assertions are not directives: their lines are skipped.
4. **The clock adapter (test side only).** EBMC treats an assertion without a clock as clocked by the design's clock. IEEE 1800-2017 16.16 leaves such an assertion without a clock, and sva2yosys rejects it. The test adds `default clocking @(posedge <clk>); endclocking` to the top module only when its concurrent assertions carry no clocking event of their own (nor inherit one: an assertion inside a `begin ... end` that an `always @(...)` governs is clocked by it, IEEE 1800-2017 16.16 c), the module has no default clocking and no other module has assertions; `<clk>` is the module's `clk`, else a new undriven wire (under SBY's synchronous model every flip-flop updates at every step, so an undriven clock behaves as EBMC assumes). Any other shape is left unchanged. sva2yosys is never changed to accept an unclocked assertion. The run reports whether it adapted the case.
5. **Mapping EBMC's answers to SBY runs.** Per property: a bounded answer (`PROVED up to bound N`) or a `REFUTED` answer of a bounded engine runs `bmc` at depth N + 1 (EBMC's bound counts transitions, SBY's depth counts states; `--bound B` plays the role of N); an unbounded `PROVED`, or an answer of an unbounded engine (`--bdd`, `--k-induction`, `--ic3`), runs `prove` with `abc pdr`; an answer of `--buechi`, or about a liveness operator, also runs the liveness flow (`sby-live`; a directive with a liveness part always does); a cover runs `cover` at depth N + 1 (41 without a bound), reached or not reached being compared with `PROVED` or `REFUTED`. Only **verdicts** are compared, never failing steps or traces. SBY reports only the assertions failing at the earliest failing step; the run is repeated for the others with the monitors of the failed ones switched off, so that every assertion has its own verdict. The liveness verdicts of a case are different: SBY's `live` mode decides a task by the first justice verdict suprove prints (SBY issue 378), so each liveness directive runs in a task of its own, the other monitors switched off. **Limit:** a directive that has several liveness parts (for example `(s_eventually a) and (s_eventually b)`) keeps them together, because the harness switches monitors on and off per directive, not per liveness part (`SVA2YOSYS_LIVE_<part>`); a `PASS` of such a directive could hide a failing part. No case of the corpus has this shape, and every liveness verdict agrees with the known EBMC answer. The design's own immediate assertions stay active in the runs, so a failure whose reported cell is not one of our monitors is an error (`failure of a non-monitor assertion <name>`) for the verdicts it leaves undecided, and a failure without a cell name is attributed to the sole remaining verdict only when the design has no immediate assertion of its own (otherwise an error).
6. **Rejected directives are isolated.** When some directives of a design are rejected and the others accepted, the rejected `assert` and `cover` statements are blanked out of the source and the others run (marked `isolated`). A rejected `assume` or `restrict` is never removed (it would change the others' verdicts): the whole case is then rejected. A directive named by the table as rejected must be rejected, whatever the other directives do.

## Classes

Each property line of the table has exactly one class; the test of the class runs the case and checks it. A `disagrees` class does not exist: a disagreement is derived by hand from IEEE 1800 and either becomes a counterexample trace case with a fix, or is classified `excluded` with its reason.

7. **`agrees`.** Our verdict equals EBMC's (assert: pass for `PROVED` and `PROVED up to bound`, fail for `REFUTED`; cover: reached for `PROVED`, not reached for `REFUTED`).
8. **`agrees-bounded`.** EBMC claims `PROVED up to bound N` and our bounded run agrees, but our liveness run fails: the infinite-trace failure of a strong sequence (IEEE 1800-2017 16.12.2), which a bounded answer does not claim. The test checks that the bounded run passes and the liveness run alone fails. The class also holds a cover for which EBMC's unbounded engine (or an answer without a bound) claims that it is never reached (`REFUTED`): our check, `cover` at the default depth 41, proves only that it is not reached within that depth, so the claim is not fully checked; the test checks that the cover is not reached. A cover that EBMC proves reachable is a witness whatever its engine and stays `agrees`.
9. **`excluded`.** EBMC's answer is not the IEEE verdict, for the reason recorded in the table (the areas of the EBMC study: pending matches, `disable iff` timing, values before the first tick, ...). The test checks that our verdict is the one the reason states, derived by hand and covered by a trace case of `reference_semantics`.
10. **`rejected <fragment>`.** sva2yosys rejects the directive (or, when it blocks the case, the case) with a message containing the fragment. A newly supported construct therefore fails the test until the table is updated; the change is reviewed, never automatic. A note after ` # ` explains an unusual entry.
11. **`skipped <reason>`.** The property is not compared, for the reason given (point 3); a case skipped as a whole has the property `-`.

## Tiers

12. A few cheap representatives (bounded and refuted, proved, cover, the excluded case, a rejected case and a skipped case) run in the **default** tier with `--external-tools=sby --external-corpora=ebmc`; every other case is `slow`, one test per case and class so that SBY runs once per case (the result of a case is kept for the session). The cases with a liveness part need `sby-live`.
